newsitem.title: INDIA: India money market inactive as Bombay banks closed.
newsitem.headline: India money market inactive as Bombay banks closed.

text.p: India's money market was closed on Wednesday as banks in Bombay, the main commercial centre, were closed for a Hindu holiday, dealers said.
Banks resume operations on Thursday but are again closed on Friday for a Moslem holiday.
The overnight call money rates closed at 0.10-0.50 percent on Tuesday on continued excess liquidity in the banking system.

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) reduced the ceiling on interest payable on deposits upto one year to 9.0 perent per annum and freed inter-bank borrowings from reserve requirements in its credit policy announcement on Tuesday.
Two state-run banks -- the State Bank of India and Corporation Bank -- immediately responded by announcing a 50 basis point cut in prime lending rate to 14.0 percent.
At a repo auction on Tuesday, the RBI cut the cut-off interest to 3.5 percent from 4.0 percent and collected 42.67 billion rupees.

Bankers said the removal of reserve requirement on inter-bank borrowings would pave the way for the development of a term money market in India and contain the sharp volatility seen in overnight call market in recent years.
